note: Implementation readings of protocol-v2.json, fixed before any outcome of v1 or v2. v1's C1-C23 apply where v2 reuses v1.

clarifications.V1: E first-cross: bar k qualifies when, over bars starting before bar k's start s_k, gain = last close / ref - 1 >= G, summed vwap x volume >= V and last close >= $1, and s_k lies in the window (the 04:00-09:30 window requires s_k < 09:30). The news variant needs a headline at or after the previous session's 16:00 with created_at <= s_k - 120 s. Entry = bar k's open at s_k; exits as v1 from bar k.
clarifications.V2: F breakout entries fill at max(bar open, level) inside the breakout bar. Because the order of that bar's high and low is unknown, exits (stops, trails, targets) start from the bar after the entry bar; Y1 and the close fallback are unchanged.
clarifications.V3: F universe: the listing exchange's official open (v1 official_price) >= 1.20 x ref, the last pre-09:30 close >= $1 and pre-09:30 dollar volume >= $250,000. A day without an official open is outside the universe (counted).
clarifications.V4: F4 VWAP: cumulative sum(vwap x volume) / sum(volume) over bars from 04:00 through the bar in question. The dip bar is the first bar starting at or after 09:35 whose close is below its VWAP; the reclaim bar is the first later bar whose close is above its VWAP; entry is the next bar's open, which must start before 11:00. Initial stop = the lowest low of bars starting 09:30 through the reclaim bar.
clarifications.V5: Y3 trail: the level is the initial stop until the running high (from the entry price, through the previous bar) reaches 1.10 x entry; from then on it is max(initial stop, 0.90 x that running high). Fills at min(level, bar open).
clarifications.V6: Y4: target = entry + 2 x (entry - stop); an open at or beyond a level exits at the open; the stop is assumed first when both fall in one bar. A stop at or above the entry (possible when the range low exceeds the entry) makes the trade exit at the next bar's open, recorded as degenerate and counted.
clarifications.V7: P uses the daily dataset for every price: fully adjusted closes, opens, highs and lows (all_*) for returns and signals, so splits between d and d+1 cancel and dividends are included; raw prices for the $1 floor and the cost price tier; dollar volume = raw vwap x raw volume. Rows with a missing d-1, d or d+1 bar are skipped (counted).
clarifications.V8: P scores: S2's 20-day high is max(all_h over the 20 sessions before d); the medians of S2 and S3 use all_v over the 20 sessions before d; S3's NR7 is all_h - all_l on d strictly below its minimum over the 6 sessions before d. Sessions with fewer than 20 prior bars are skipped for S2 and S3.
clarifications.V9: P costs: entry at the close pays 0.5 x the half-spread of bucket 10:00-16:00 for its price tier and day d's dollar-volume tier; Z1's exit pays 0.5 x the 09:30-10:00 bucket and Z2's 0.5 x the 10:00-16:00 bucket, using day d+1's price tier and day d's dollar-volume tier; Z3 uses the one it exits at. Fees as v1 at the exit date. Trade-level notional $20,000.
clarifications.V10: P capture: the day-d+1 degree tier uses all_c(d+1) / all_c(d) - 1 over every universe row; recall = selected-and-in-tier / in-tier, reported for the qualifying set and for the top-5 set, beside the tier's base rate.
clarifications.V11: Portfolio for P: equity marked at day d's close equals the session's starting equity (positions opened at the close and closed the next day before the next entry); gross leverage = min(2, rung x regime x drawdown factor). Family E and F portfolios are v1's, with a decision-time dollar volume cap.
clarifications.V12: Bootstrap seed = int.from_bytes(sha256(b'mover-followup-v2-20260924').digest()[:8], 'big'); each family's rule-exits share one replicate matrix per split; P's calendar is its entry sessions d.
clarifications.V13: Portfolio slots for E and F are filled in entry-time order (then symbol), at most 5 per session, because a live system cannot rank later fires; notional comes from the session's starting equity. P slots rank day d's dollar volume (then symbol). A P trade needs both d and d+1 inside the split, so no trade exits into a later split.
clarifications.V14: P signals use day d's full regular session (close, high, volume), which a live system only approximates at the closing-auction order cutoff; the paper mapping scores a snapshot about 10 minutes before the cutoff and records the difference. This is a limitation of the historical test, not a correction.
